Finite representation type

Words: 45
Module theory OurBigBook.com
A finite-dimensional algebra has finite representation type when there are only finitely many isomorphism classes of finite-dimensional indecomposable modules. This counts module types, not the dimensions or the number of direct sums formed from them. For a block of a group algebra, finite representation type is equivalent to a cyclic defect group of a block.

Auslander–Reiten quiver

Words: 103 Articles: 1
Module theory OurBigBook.com
For a finite-dimensional algebra, the Auslander–Reiten quiver has one vertex for each isomorphism class of finite-dimensional indecomposable modules, and its arrows record irreducible module homomorphisms. A homomorphism is irreducible when it is neither a split injection nor a split surjection and every factorization forces the first map to split injectively or the second to split surjectively.

Stable Auslander–Reiten quiver (Γs​(A))

Words: 48
Auslander–Reiten quiver OurBigBook.com
For a self-injective finite-dimensional algebra, remove the projective vertices from its Auslander–Reiten quiver. The resulting stable quiver has vertices the nonprojective indecomposable modules. Its translation sends the end term of an almost-split exact sequence to its start term. In particular a quiver of shape ZAs​/⟨τe⟩ has es vertices.

Topological group module

Words: 39
Module theory OurBigBook.com
A topological abelian group A with a continuous action of a topological group G by group automorphisms. Continuity means joint continuity of G×A→A. For a discrete coefficient group this is equivalent to every element of A having an open stabilizer.

Character module (M∗=HomZ​(M,Q/Z))

Words: 44
Module theory OurBigBook.com
For a module M over a commutative ring A, its character module is the additive-group dual into D=Q/Z, with action (aϕ)(m)=ϕ(am). The group D is an injective cogenerator of abelian groups. The natural adjunction HomA​(N,M∗)≅HomZ​(N⊗A​M,D) sends h to the balanced pairing (n,m)↦h(n)(m).

Representation of an associative algebra (ρ:A→Endk​(V))

Words: 375 Articles: 6
Module theory OurBigBook.com
An algebra representation is a unital algebra homomorphism into the endomorphisms of a vector space. It is equivalent to making that vector space a left module over the algebra, with av=ρ(a)v.

Representation of a Banach algebra (π:A→EndC​(X))

Words: 350 Articles: 5
Representation of an associative algebra OurBigBook.com
A representation of a complex Banach algebra is a complex-linear multiplicative action on a vector space. For a unital action require π(1)=I; a nonunital algebra can be handled by extending the action to its unitization. A nonzero action is algebraically irreducible when it has no nonzero proper invariant vector subspace, equivalently when it defines a simple module.

Algebraically irreducible representation of a Banach algebra

Words: 188 Articles: 2
Representation of a Banach algebra OurBigBook.com
Algebraic irreducibility excludes every proper nonzero invariant vector subspace, including those that are not closed. It is stronger than topological irreducibility, which excludes only closed invariant subspaces. For a nonzero irreducible action, every nonzero vector is cyclic in the algebraic sense: Aξ=X.
Countable annihilation sequence in an irreducible Banach module (π(am​⋯a1​)ξn​=0 (m>n))
Words: 68
Algebraically irreducible representation of a Banach algebra OurBigBook.com
For countably many linearly independent vectors in an infinite-dimensional irreducible complex Banach module, there are elements an​ satisfying the displayed annihilation conditions while the tail images {π(an​⋯a1​)ξj​:j≥n} remain linearly independent. Use the quotient norm on an irreducible Banach module to make each finite annihilator a closed Banach subspace. The Jacobson density theorem makes each condition of independence of finitely many tail images open and dense there; the Baire category theorem intersects these countably many conditions. This is stronger than prescribing only finitely many images once.
Quotient norm on an irreducible Banach module (∥π(a)ξ∥0​=infb∈Lξ​​∥a+b∥)
Words: 81
Algebraically irreducible representation of a Banach algebra OurBigBook.com
For a unital irreducible action and ξ=0, the annihilator Lξ​={a:π(a)ξ=0} is a maximal left ideal and is closed. Thus A/Lξ​ supplies the displayed complete norm on the module, with contractive action. Every module endomorphism is bounded for this quotient norm: its value at the cyclic vector is aξ, so it is induced by bounded right multiplication by a on the quotient. The Gelfand-Mazur theorem then makes the module's commutant consist of scalar operators. This constructs one compatible norm; it does not by itself establish continuity in a different preassigned norm.

Normed representation of a Banach algebra (π(A)⊆B(X))

Words: 110 Articles: 1
Representation of a Banach algebra OurBigBook.com
A normed representation acts by individually bounded operators on a normed vector space. This condition alone does not assume that a↦π(a) is continuous in the operator norm, nor that the representation space is complete. A continuous representation has a common bound ∥π(a)∥≤C∥a∥.
Johnson's continuity theorem for irreducible normed representations (∥π(a)∥≤C∥a∥)
Words: 73
Normed representation of a Banach algebra OurBigBook.com
Every algebraically irreducible representation of a Banach algebra that is normed is continuous. The continuous orbit vectors form an invariant subspace. If all nonzero orbit maps were discontinuous, apply the countable annihilation sequence in an irreducible Banach module and the gliding-hump continuity principle to right multiplication on the algebra and evaluation of the operator-valued representation. Off-diagonal maps vanish, whereas diagonal maps are discontinuous, a contradiction. Once every orbit map is continuous, the Uniform boundedness principle on the Banach algebra gives the common operator-norm bound. Completing the original normed representation space supplies the Banach operator space needed in the argument.

Degeneration of a module (X⇝Y)

Words: 61
Module theory OurBigBook.com
A finite-dimensional module X degenerates to Y when Y has a representative in the closure of X's change-of-basis orbit in the representation variety of an associative algebra. The full orbit of Y then lies in that closure. The relation is transitive because orbit closures are closed and invariant under change of basis. A split extension as a degeneration shows that a module degenerates to the direct sum of its composition factors.

Hereditary ring

Words: 175 Articles: 2
Module theory OurBigBook.com
A ring is left hereditary if every submodule of a left projective module is projective. Equivalently, every left module has a projective resolution of length at most one. The standard projective resolution of a quiver representation, used also for arbitrary infinite-dimensional modules, proves that path algebras are left hereditary.

Basic hereditary algebra path-algebra theorem (A≅kQ)

Words: 93
Hereditary ring OurBigBook.com
Let A be a finite-dimensional basic algebra over an algebraically closed field and a hereditary ring. The radicals of its indecomposable projectives are projective and satisfy JPi​≅⨁j​Pjaij​​, where aij​ are the Ext quiver arrow multiplicities. Hence dimPi​=1+∑j​aij​dimPj​, forcing strict dimension decrease along arrows and therefore acyclicity. Lifting an arrow basis in J/J2 gives a surjective path algebra homomorphism kQ→A. The number of paths starting at i satisfies the same dimension recursion. Equality of total dimensions proves the homomorphism is an isomorphism. Sums of vertex idempotents over connected components are precisely the primitive central idempotents, so components give the blocks.

Path algebras are hereditary (ExtkQn​(V,W)=0(n≥2))

Words: 45
Hereditary ring OurBigBook.com
The standard projective resolution of a quiver representation has length one, even for quivers with oriented cycles. Thus every path algebra is a hereditary ring, and higher extension groups vanish. Applying a long exact sequence of Ext groups to 0→I→K→C→0 gives a surjection Ext1(K,W)↠Ext1(I,W), since the next term Ext2(C,W) is zero. This is the hereditary step in the Ringel lemma on bricks.

Regular sequence on a module (ti​:M/(t1​,…,ti−1​)M↪M/(t1​,…,ti−1​)M)

Words: 39
Module theory OurBigBook.com
For central elements, each multiplication map on the preceding quotient must be injective; a usual convention also requires the final quotient to be nonzero. The augmented Koszul complex on central ring elements tensored with M is then a quasi-isomorphism to the final quotient in degree zero.

Composition series of a module (0=M0​⊂M1​⊂⋯⊂Mr​=M)

Words: 57 Articles: 1
Module theory OurBigBook.com
A composition series of a module is a finite chain of submodules whose nonzero successive quotient modules are simple modules. Every finite-dimensional Lie algebra representation has such a chain, viewed as a module over the universal enveloping algebra.

Composition factor (Mi​/Mi−1​)

Words: 30
Composition series of a module OurBigBook.com
A composition factor is an irreducible successive quotient in a composition series of a module. For a central Casimir operator, its scalar on a composition factor is an eigenvalue of the operator on the original Lie algebra representation.

Uniform module

Words: 154 Articles: 2
Module theory OurBigBook.com
A nonzero module is uniform if every pair of nonzero submodules has nonzero intersection. Equivalently, every nonzero submodule is an essential submodule. A right Noetherian domain is uniform as a right module: if aA∩bA=0 for nonzero a,b, the right ideals biaA, i≥0, form an infinite direct sum, contradicting the ascending chain condition.

Uniform dimension (udimM)

Words: 51
Uniform module OurBigBook.com
The uniform dimension of a module is the supremum of the numbers of nonzero submodules that can occur in an internal direct sum. Finite uniform dimension is equivalent to having no infinite internal direct sum of nonzero submodules. A finite direct sum of uniform modules contained as an essential submodule gives that number as the dimension. The finite uniform decomposition of a Noetherian module therefore gives finite uniform dimension.

Finite uniform decomposition of a Noetherian module

Words: 59
Uniform module OurBigBook.com
Every nonzero Noetherian module contains a uniform module: otherwise repeatedly split a nonuniform nonzero submodule into two disjoint nonzero submodules, retaining one and collecting the other, to build an infinite direct sum. Repeatedly adding a uniform submodule disjoint from the current finite sum must likewise stop. The final finite sum is an essential submodule, since any disjoint nonzero submodule would allow another addition.

Indecomposable module

Words: 124 Articles: 1
Module theory OurBigBook.com
A nonzero module is indecomposable if it cannot be expressed as a direct sum of two nonzero submodules. The zero module is excluded. A module of finite composition length is indecomposable exactly when its endomorphism ring has no idempotents other than zero and one: an idempotent splits the module into its image and kernel.

Top of an indecomposable projective module (P/PJ(A))

Words: 82
Indecomposable module OurBigBook.com
For a nonzero finitely generated indecomposable module P that is a projective module over a right Artinian ring A, its top P/PJ(A) is a simple module. The Jacobson radical J(A) is a nilpotent ideal, so the top is nonzero; the quotient is a semisimple module over the semisimple ring A/J(A). If it decomposed, a nontrivial idempotent of its endomorphism ring would lift by projectivity to an endomorphism of P. The Hopkins-Levitzki theorem gives finite composition length, and the Fitting lemma makes the lift either invertible or nilpotent. Its induced map on the top would have the same property, impossible for that nontrivial idempotent.

Fitting lemma

Words: 33
Module theory OurBigBook.com
For an endomorphism f of a finite-length module M, sufficiently large n gives
M=ker(fn)⊕im(fn).
(1)
If M is indecomposable, every endomorphism is therefore either invertible or nilpotent, so its endomorphism ring is local.

Krull–Schmidt theorem

Words: 57 Articles: 1
Module theory OurBigBook.com
The Krull–Schmidt theorem says that a finite-length module decomposes as a finite direct sum of indecomposable modules, uniquely up to permutation and isomorphism of the summands.

Krull-Schmidt decomposition (X≅⨁a​Ma⊕ma​​)

Words: 31
Krull–Schmidt theorem OurBigBook.com
A finite-dimensional module is ⨁a​Ma⊕ma​​ with pairwise nonisomorphic indecomposables and uniquely determined multiplicities. The Fitting lemma makes their endomorphism rings local. The multiplicity spaces provide the general linear factors in the Levi decomposition of a quiver automorphism group.

Dual module (M∗)

Words: 35 Articles: 1
Module theory OurBigBook.com
For an R-module M, its dual module is M∗=HomR​(M,R), with pointwise addition and scalar multiplication.

Double dual module (M∗∗)

Words: 17
Dual module OurBigBook.com
The double dual module is M∗∗=HomR​(M∗,R). The evaluation homomorphism sends m∈M to the functional f↦f(m).

Finitely generated module

Words: 238 Articles: 3
Module theory OurBigBook.com
An R-module is finitely generated when there are finitely many elements m1​,…,mr​ such that every element is an R-linear combination of them.

Minimal number of generators of a module (μA​(M)=dimA/m​(M/mM)(M finite, A local))

Words: 111
Finitely generated module OurBigBook.com
For a module M, μA​(M) is the least cardinality of a generating set, equivalently the least size of a basis of a free module surjecting onto M. If (A,m) is a local ring and M is finitely generated, then μA​(M)=dimA/m​(M/mM). Any generating set spans this quotient, proving the lower bound. Lift a basis of the quotient and let J be the submodule generated by those lifts. Then N=M/J is finitely generated and satisfies N=mN. For generators ni​ write ni​=∑j​cij​nj​ with cij​∈m. The adjugate of I−C shows that det(I−C) annihilates N; this determinant is one modulo m and hence a unit. Thus N=0, giving the upper bound.

Clearing denominators relative to an independent module subset (0=r∈R,rM⊆⟨T⟩)

Words: 49
Finitely generated module OurBigBook.com
Let a finitely generated module over an integral domain have a finite generating set S and a maximal independent subset T. For each s∈/T, dependence of T∪{s} gives a nonzero coefficient as​ with as​s∈⟨T⟩. The product of those coefficients is nonzero and carries the whole module into ⟨T⟩.

Finite generation as a quotient of a finite free module

Words: 54
Finitely generated module OurBigBook.com
An R-module is finitely generated exactly when it is the image of a surjection from a finite free module Rn. Given generators mi​, send (ri​) to ∑i​ri​mi​; conversely, the images of the standard free generators generate every such image. This criterion does not assert that the module is free: a quotient can have nontrivial relations.

Artinian module

Words: 131 Articles: 2
Module theory OurBigBook.com
An R-module is Artinian when every descending chain of submodules stabilizes. Equivalently, every nonempty family of submodules has a minimal member.

Artinian modules are co-Hopfian (f injective⟹f surjective)

Words: 38
Artinian module OurBigBook.com
For an injective module endomorphism f:M→M of an Artinian module, the chain M⊇fM⊇f2M⊇⋯ stabilizes. If fnM=fn+1M, then every x satisfies fnx=fn+1y. Injectivity of fn gives x=fy, proving surjectivity. No finite-length or Noetherian hypothesis is needed.

Artinian modules in a short exact sequence

Words: 71
Artinian module OurBigBook.com
For a short exact sequence 0→N→M→Q→0, the middle module is Artinian exactly when both outer modules are Artinian. Submodules and quotients inherit the descending chain condition. Conversely, for a descending chain Mi​, both Mi​∩N and its image in Q eventually stabilize. If x∈Mi​, choose y∈Mi+1​ with the same image in Q; then x−y∈Mi​∩N=Mi+1​∩N, giving Mi​=Mi+1​. Induction shows that finite direct sums of Artinian modules are Artinian.

Filtered colimit of modules

Words: 128 Articles: 4
Module theory OurBigBook.com
A filtered colimit of modules is a direct limit indexed by a filtered category. Filtered colimits preserve exact sequences, and tensor products commute with them.

Direct system of abelian groups

Words: 103 Articles: 3
Filtered colimit of modules OurBigBook.com
A direct system indexed by a directed set A consists of abelian groups Ga​ and homomorphisms ϕab​:Ga​→Gb​ for a≤b, with ϕaa​=1 and ϕbc​ϕab​=ϕac​.

Direct limit of abelian groups (lim​a​Ga​)

Words: 80 Articles: 2
Direct system of abelian groups OurBigBook.com
The direct limit of a direct system of abelian groups is the quotient of ⨁a​Ga​ by the relations identifying g∈Ga​ with ϕab​(g)∈Gb​ whenever a≤b.
Sequential direct limit of multiplication maps on the integers (lim​(Za0​​Za1​​⋯))
Words: 57 Articles: 1
Direct limit of abelian groups OurBigBook.com
For nonzero integers ai​ and Pn​=a0​⋯an−1​, the compatible embeddings of stage n into Q send m to m/Pn​. They identify the direct limit with
⋃n≥0​Pn−1​Z⊆Q.
(2)
Rational group with square-free denominators (Qsq​)
Words: 26
Sequential direct limit of multiplication maps on the integers OurBigBook.com
The additive group Qsq​ consists of the rational numbers whose reduced denominators are square-free integers. If p0​,p1​,… lists the primes without repetition, then
Qsq​≅lim​(Zp0​​Zp1​​Zp2​​⋯).
(3)

Bimodule

Words: 20
Module theory OurBigBook.com
An (R,S)-bimodule is simultaneously a left R-module and a right S-module, with commuting scalar actions (rm)s=r(ms).

Invariant submodule (MG)

Words: 22
Module theory OurBigBook.com
For a group G acting on a module M, the invariant submodule is MG={m∈M:g⋅m=m for all g∈G}.

Coinvariant module (MG​)

Words: 76 Articles: 1
Module theory OurBigBook.com
For a group G acting on a module M, the coinvariant module is
MG​=M/⟨g⋅m−m:g∈G, m∈M⟩.
(4)

Abelianization over a Zp-extension (Gab:XΓ​=X/(γ−1)X)

Words: 56
Coinvariant module OurBigBook.com
Suppose 1→X→G→Γ→1 is an exact sequence of pro-p groups, with X abelian and Γ≅Zp​. Conjugation gives X a compact Galois module structure. The closed commutator subgroup is (γ−1)X: its image is closed by compactness, and after quotienting by it, a lift of γ centralizes X and topologically generates the remaining quotient. Hence 0→XΓ​→Gab→Γ→0 is exact.

Support of a module

Words: 26
Module theory OurBigBook.com
The support of an R-module M is
SuppR​(M)={p∈SpecR:Mp​=0}.
(5)
For a nonzero finitely generated module, the support is nonempty and contains a maximal ideal.

Good filtration of a module OurBigBook.com
For a good filtration of a module over a fixed finite-dimensional filtration of a ring whose associated graded algebra is commutative and finitely generated, the cumulative Hilbert function is eventually a quasipolynomial by the Hilbert-Serre theorem. If the associated graded algebra is a standard graded algebra, the Hilbert function is eventually polynomial. Two good module filtrations bound one another after fixed shifts, so they have the same growth degree. Set d(0)=−∞. For the Bernstein filtration this is the Bernstein growth dimension of a Weyl algebra module.

This is the degree-one convention for an almost commutative algebra: the exhaustive filtration is generated by a finite-dimensional first step containing 1, the degree-zero part is k, and its associated graded algebra is commutative. The first step is a finite-dimensional Lie algebra under commutators. Its inclusion into A extends by the universal property to a surjection from its universal enveloping algebra. The element 1 of the first step is retained as a central Lie generator and its image is the associative identity; quotienting the first step by k1 before taking the bracket can lose scalar commutators. Endomorphism ring OurBigBook.com
An endomorphism ring is local when its nonunits form a proper two-sided ideal; commutativity is not required. The Fitting lemma gives this property for an indecomposable finite-length module. If two nonunits had an invertible sum, multiplication by its inverse would give I=f+g with noninvertible f,g. Fitting makes f nilpotent, so I−f=g would be invertible, a contradiction. Products with a nonunit are nonunits by finite-length injectivity/surjectivity. The quotient by the nonunit ideal is a division ring.

Endomorphism ring OurBigBook.com
For a finite-dimensional module over an algebraically closed field, write a Krull-Schmidt decomposition X=⨁a​Ma⊕ma​​ with distinct indecomposable types. Each endomorphism ring of Ma​ is a local endomorphism ring with residue division algebra k, by the finite-dimensional division algebra over an algebraically closed field result. Modulo the Jacobson radical of End(X), the blocks of one type become Mma​​(k) and all maps between different types vanish. A composite through a different indecomposable type cannot be invertible, since that would make one type a direct summand of the other. This yields the displayed product and the Levi decomposition of a quiver automorphism group.

Proof of Ringel lemma on bricks
Words: 117
Ringel lemma on bricks OurBigBook.com
The Fitting lemma supplies a nonzero nilpotent endomorphism f of a non-brick indecomposable X. Minimize its nonzero rank; nilpotence and minimality give f2=0. Set I=imf⊂K=kerf=⨁j​Kj​. Choose a nonzero component u:I→Kj​. The square-zero endomorphism Xf​Iu​Kj​↪X has rank at least dimI, so u is injective.
If Ext1(I,Kj​)=0, the projection K→Kj​ extends to X→Kj​ by the long exact sequence of Ext groups, giving a module retraction and contradicting indecomposability. Thus this extension group is nonzero. Since path algebras are hereditary, u induces a surjection Ext1(Kj​,Kj​)↠Ext1(I,Kj​). Hence Kj​ is a proper indecomposable submodule with self-extensions. Iterate until a brick module is reached; dimensions strictly decrease.
This minimal-rank argument is given in section 2 of William Crawley-Boevey's quiver lectures.

Free module OurBigBook.com
Order the linearly independent subsets of a vector space by inclusion. A chain's union is independent, since every finite relation is contained in one chain member. Zorn's lemma gives a maximal independent subset. A vector outside its span could be adjoined while preserving independence, so it spans. Sending finite-support coefficient families to their linear combinations gives an isomorphism from the free module on that subset to V. This supplies an arbitrary, possibly infinite-dimensional basis using the axiom of choice; no pre-existing basis theorem is invoked.

Free module OurBigBook.com
Elements of a module are linearly independent if every finite linear relation between them has all coefficients zero. An independent finite set freely generates its span, a finite free module. A module P is projective when every map from P through the target of a surjection lifts through that surjection.

Projective module OurBigBook.com
A projective module is a direct summand of a free module. Free modules are flat because tensoring with a free module produces a direct sum of copies of the original module and map. If F=P⊕Q is flat, tensoring an injection with F is the direct sum of its tensor maps with P and Q, so each component is injective. Applying this to a free module containing P proves that P is flat.

Every module P is a quotient of a free module F=⨁p∈P​Aep​, via ep​↦p. If P is a projective module, lift 1P​ through this surjection to obtain a section s:P→F. The resulting split short exact sequence identifies F with kerπ⊕P. Conversely, if P is a summand of a free module, extend a prescribed map out of P to the free module using the summand projection, lift each basis image through the given surjection, and restrict the lift to P. This proves the equivalence with the lifting definition of a projective module, for arbitrary ranks.

For a finite-dimensional algebra A, a principal indecomposable module is an indecomposable direct summand of the left regular module, equivalently Ae for a primitive idempotent e. Its head of a module is simple, and it is the projective cover of that simple module.

Projective module OurBigBook.com
A finite projective module is a finitely generated module that is a projective module. Equivalently it is a direct summand of a finite free module: a finite free surjection splits by projectivity. Its dual module is finite projective and its evaluation map to its double dual module is an isomorphism, since both properties hold for finite free modules and pass to direct summands. Finite generation is needed for this elementary duality argument.

Words: 112 Articles: 1
Projective module OurBigBook.com
An invertible module over a commutative ring A is a finitely generated module that is a projective module and whose localization at a prime ideal is free of rank one at every prime. Its dual module L∗=HomA​(L,A) is also finite projective. Evaluation L⊗A​L∗→A is an isomorphism after every prime localization, hence is an isomorphism globally by localization detects zero elements. The Picard group of a ring consists of the isomorphism classes of these modules under the tensor product of modules.

Invertible module OurBigBook.com
For a ring homomorphism A→B, extension of scalars takes an invertible module to an invertible B-module. A direct-summand presentation in a finite free module remains a direct-summand presentation after tensoring. At a prime q⊂B contracting to p, localization gives Bq​⊗Ap​​Lp​≅Bq​. Compatibility with tensor products, identities and composition makes the Picard group of a ring a covariant functor.

Words: 417 Articles: 5
Projective module OurBigBook.com
For a nonzero module, the projective dimension pdR​M is the shortest length of a projective resolution of the module M, or infinity if no finite projective resolution exists. Equivalently, it is the supremum of degrees with nonzero ExtRn​(M,N) as N ranges over all modules. This equivalence follows by dimension shifting and the characterization of projective modules by vanishing Ext1.

Words: 274 Articles: 2
Projective dimension OurBigBook.com
Let M be a nonzero finitely generated module over a commutative Noetherian ring. Take a length-n resolution with finite projective terms. If its top Ext functor with coefficients in A vanished, the dual of its last injection would be surjective. The dual of a finite projective module is projective, so that surjection splits. Finite projective modules are isomorphic to their double duals, so dualizing gives a splitting of the original injection. The resolution then shortens, contradicting minimality of n. When n=0, a nonzero coordinate of a finite free module containing M as a summand gives a nonzero map M→A.

Words: 90
Top Ext detects finite projective dimension OurBigBook.com
For a nonzero left finitely generated module over a left Noetherian ring, take a finite projective resolution with finite projective modules. Vanishing of its top Ext functor would make the dual of its final injection surjective. These duals are right finite projective modules, so the surjection splits. Dualizing back and using finite projective double dual modules splits the original injection and shortens the resolution, contradicting the definition of projective dimension. When the dimension is zero, a coordinate map of a finite free module containing the nonzero projective summand supplies a nonzero map to R. The left/right distinction in the duals is essential for a noncommutative ring.

Put A=k[[t]] and K=A[1/t]. A free resolution has countably many generators ei​ and relations ei​−tei+1​. Applying the Hom functor with coefficients in A gives (bi​)↦(bi​−tbi+1​) on sequence products. This is surjective: for prescribed (ci​) use bi​=∑j≥0​tjci+j​, a well-defined formal power series. Therefore the degree-one Ext functor vanishes. But HomA​(K,A)=0, since every image is infinitely divisible by t. A nonzero projective module has a nonzero coordinate map into A, so K is not projective. Its displayed resolution proves that its projective dimension is exactly one. The finite-generation hypothesis in top Ext detects finite projective dimension is essential.

The global dimension of a ring is the supremum of the projective dimensions of all its modules, allowing infinity. It measures the longest projective resolution needed by any module. For a field it is zero, since every module is a vector space and hence free.

Words: 53
Global dimension OurBigBook.com
If global dimension is zero, every module is a projective module. Each short exact sequence splits because its quotient is projective. Conversely, splitting every short exact sequence makes each module a direct summand of a free module and therefore a projective module. Splitting also makes every module an injective module: for A↪B choose a retraction B→A and compose it with any prescribed map out of A.

If A is a finite module over a commutative central subring R and M is a simple left A-module, then M=Am is finite over R.
